verdict.rationale: SharePoint documents a broad first-party REST service and Microsoft Graph surface. It covers CRUD on files and folders, PUT/MERGE updates, recycle operations, read-write lists, listItems and driveItems, tenant settings, and $batch, so much of the UI's core data work can be done through the API. Nothing in the evidence claims or shows full UI-to-API parity. missing for 10: an explicit documented claim of UI/API parity, API coverage evidence for page authoring, permissions and site administration, and independent hands-on confirmation that UI-only gaps don't exist.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Now, developers can interact remotely with SharePoint data by using any technology that supports REST web requests.
Perform basic CRUD operations on folders and files with the SharePoint REST interface.
Use **PUT** and **MERGE** operations to update existing SharePoint objects.
